_meta.purpose: Authoritative machine-readable capability catalog for all 60 benchmarks: what ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE and the fill-pattern parameter can actually change, per-pattern type-safety and domain-validity, adapter feasibility, and >4096 cause classification. AUDIT METADATA ONLY after E1: nothing in the productive spec pipeline reads or enforces this catalog yet - enforcement (effective_patterns(benchmark) = globally_offered INTERSECT benchmark_supported) is a documented E2 target.
_meta.effectiveness_rule: A pattern counts as EFFECTIVE only if it can actually change the task-relevant benchmark input. Distinct pattern names/spec_keys/rationales alone are NOT test diversity; a pattern-labeled spec on a benchmark without a reachable fill hook is STRUCTURALLY_NO_PATTERN_EFFECT (structural finding; input-byte identity was not execution-proven and is not claimed).

harness_facts.dtype_deduction: ENHANCED_FILL(x, lo, hi) deduces the pattern value type DType from the lo/hi ARGUMENTS, not from the container's value_type (enhanced-fill.hpp:173-174); pattern values are converted by assignment x[i] = <DType value>. In-container probe (g++ 13.3, -O3): vector<int> with 0.0/100.0 literals -> DType=double; extreme_values/spike_at compute DBL_MAX-scale doubles whose conversion to int is undefined behavior (observed saturation, formally UB). Runtime and define mode share the same deduction; only the value_range override path saturates (runtime) / constant-folds (define).
harness_facts.pattern_reach: Patterns affect only ENHANCED_FILL containers; fillRandString/fillRandWithZeroes/fillRandDirectedGraph/hand-rolled rand() loops/sparse D4-D5 builders are outside the pattern axis.

open_e2_policy_decisions.EXTREME_PATTERN_SEMANTICS: OPEN - Option A: element-type extrema (numeric_limits<DType>); Option B: extrema of the declared benchmark/fill domain (derivable from call-site lo/hi at every audited site). Suite impact: with Option A, extreme_values is deterministically BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE-only on the tripwired/overflowing benchmarks (histogram 20/21/24, scan 33, stencil 51, reduce 26 all_zeros/spike, fft 05/07/08/09, dense_la 00/02/03/04, sparse 46/47 partially, stencil 52/53 interior) and executes oracle-side signed-overflow UB on scan/34, stencil/54, transform/58, graph/17 (hypothetical); Option B is benign nearly everywhere but reduces extreme_values to the alternating pattern at lo/hi.
open_e2_policy_decisions.VALUE_RANGE_DOMAIN_POLICY: OPEN - spec value_range overrides are validated only for lo<=hi (specs.py:309-319): they can leave frozen domains (-> tripwire BI-only runs), exceed element-type ranges (define path constant-fold saturates; runtime path saturates; the DEDUCED-DType UB on mismatched sites remains), and produce formally-valid but methodically worthless specs. Existing specs already violate frozen domains via explicit_values on reduce/28 (negative values) and histogram/24 (negative and 2^31 values).

type_unsafe_fill_sites.notes: THE type-unsafe site of the family: DType deduced from the DOUBLE literals, elements are int, so every pattern value is computed as double and converted at x[i] = <double>. In [0,100] that is defined truncation (random/ramps/alternating/all_same=50.0/duplicate/sorted_except_one all fine), but extreme_values (+-DBL_MAX), spike_at (DBL_MAX/2) and any out-of-int-range explicit_values line produce out-of-range double->int conversion = UNDEFINED BEHAVIOR (observed saturation to INT_MIN/INT_MAX, formally UB). The Wave-2B guard fires only AFTER this conversion - it is a domain gate, not a UB fix. Fix: int literals ENHANCED_FILL(x, 0, 100) -> DType=int -> extremes become INT_MIN/INT_MAX type-safely.

TYPE-UNSAFE SITE: double literals -100.0/100.0 deduce DType=double for a vector<float>. extreme_values computes +-DBL_MAX and spike_at computes DBL_MAX/2, both outside float's representable range; the implicit double->float conversion on assignment x[i]=<double> is formally UB ([conv.double]) - in practice IEEE +-inf. In-range patterns (ramps, alternating, all_same, all_zeros, random) convert double->float losslessly enough and are fine. Fix: use -100.0f/100.0f so DType=float (extrema become +-FLT_MAX, spike FLT_MAX/2 - all representable).

DType deduced double from the double literals but the container is vector<float>: extreme_values computes +-DBL_MAX and spike_at computes DBL_MAX/2 in double, then assigns to float — out-of-range double->float conversion is UNDEFINED BEHAVIOR (practically saturates to +-inf on IEEE targets). explicit_values (cyclic doubles) is likewise unclamped: any spec value beyond +-FLT_MAX reproduces the UB. All in-range patterns (ramp/alternating/mid/random over [-100,100]) are safe. Fix: use -100.0f/100.0f literals to deduce DType=float (extrema then +-FLT_MAX, spike FLT_MAX/2 — finite in float).

DType=double on a vector<float>: extreme_values computes +-DBL_MAX and spike_at DBL_MAX/2 in double, assigned to float — out-of-range double->float conversion = UNDEFINED BEHAVIOR (practically +-inf). Downstream, sameRecordMultiset compares the float field with reportAndCompareEq (cpu.cc:91-93): a non-finite REFERENCE-side value triggers mismatchNoteNonFiniteReference() -> BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE and the index is skipped (utilities.hpp:425-428). Fix: -1.0f/1.0f literals (DType=float; extremes +-FLT_MAX, spike FLT_MAX/2, finite).

The fill ASSIGNMENT itself is int->int (no conversion UB). type_safe=false because an offered pattern reaches real UB downstream with NO guard: extreme_values writes INT_MIN/INT_MAX cells and the UNGUARDED oracle sums raw neighbor values into int (baseline.hpp:27-51) - e.g. the two vertical neighbors share the extreme pattern's index parity for even N (and same-sign pairs exist for odd N via the diagonals), so sum += INT_MIN twice is signed-overflow UB. Unlike sibling 51 there is no in-domain scan in cpu.cc. Random-based patterns draw {0,1} (hi-exclusive fillRand, utilities.hpp:160); alternating/ramp inject the value 2 (defined, see domain).

benchmarks.size_rationale: All three validate() buffers A/A_correct/A_test are TEST_SIZE*TEST_SIZE (cpu.cc:53-55) and both oracle and candidate are called with TEST_SIZE (cpu.cc:68,72). No static-sized component remains. Static spec sizes 0/1/2/7 are safe: correctLuFactorize with N=0 or 1 does no division (baseline.hpp:13-23) and enhancedFillPattern early-returns on n==0 (enhanced-fill.hpp:177-179).
benchmarks.pattern_rationale: The one and only validate() input (A) is fully ENHANCED_FILL-controlled (cpu.cc:63); every offered pattern changes the entire graded computation. Caveat: pattern choice being EFFECTIVE mechanically does not mean every pattern is mathematically meaningful for unpivoted LU (see domain_restrictions).
benchmarks.input_construction: Single input matrix A (TEST_SIZE^2 doubles) filled via ENHANCED_FILL(A, -10.0, 10.0) at cpu.cc:63, then copied to A_correct/A_test (cpu.cc:67,71). Oracle correctLuFactorize is unpivoted in-place Doolittle LU (baseline.hpp:13-23). Comparison: reportAndCompare(A_correct, A_test, 1e-3, A) (cpu.cc:76) - 4-arg form passes A only for mismatch reporting; ABSOLUTE tolerance |a-b|>1e-3 (utilities.hpp:482).

fill_sites.conversion_notes: double literals -> DType=double == value_type; extreme_values assigns +-DBL_MAX and spike_at DBL_MAX/2, all representable in double - no conversion, no UB. value_range override casts to decltype(lo)=double (enhanced-fill.hpp:450-453), lossless.

benchmarks.other_input_constructors: none in validate(); timed path reset() uses fillRand(A,-10,10) (cpu.cc:28) which is outside the pattern axis by design

domain.summary: Implicit and structural: A must be factorizable WITHOUT pivoting - every pivot arising during elimination must be nonzero and well-scaled. Oracle has no pivoting and no zero-pivot guard (baseline.hpp:16: factor = A[i*N+k]/A[k*N+k]; 0/0 -> NaN, x/0 -> Inf). The frozen random range [-10,10] satisfies this w.h.p.; structured patterns generally do NOT: all_zeros, all_same (midpoint of -10/10 is exactly 0 -> identical to all_zeros here), alternating (identical rows for even N -> exactly singular, NaN at second pivot), extreme_values (identical +-DBL_MAX rows -> zero rows after step 0, 0/0=NaN at k=1), ascending/descending/sorted_except_one (rank-2-in-exact-arithmetic ramps -> near-zero pivots, huge growth, likely Inf/NaN or absolute-tolerance blowup). duplicate_at and random are benign w.h.p.

The frozen random range [-10,10] satisfies this w.h.p.; structured patterns generally do NOT: all_zeros, all_same (midpoint of -10/10 is exactly 0 -> identical to all_zeros here), alternating (identical rows for even N -> exactly singular, NaN at second pivot), extreme_values (identical +-DBL_MAX rows -> zero rows after step 0, 0/0=NaN at k=1), ascending/descending/sorted_except_one (rank-2-in-exact-arithmetic ramps -> near-zero pivots, huge growth, likely Inf/NaN or absolute-tolerance blowup). duplicate_at and random are benign w.h.p.
tripwires: none - no BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE guard exists in this cpu.cc (repo grep: only reduce/26, utilities.hpp, harness-markers.hpp contain the token). The harness-level non_finite_reference marker (utilities.hpp:363-378, emitted from reportAndCompareSelectedWith at utilities.hpp:425-428) fires whenever the ORACLE result is non-finite at a graded index; the index is then skipped. Patterns that fire it here: all_zeros, all_same, alternating, extreme_values (deterministically); ascending/descending/sorted_except_one (near-singular, likely). These are baseline-gate-only signals, not model failures.

benchmarks.value_range_risk: lo/hi are double literals; ENHANCED_FILL_LO/HI overrides cast to double - no narrowing/UB. Real risk is numeric: tolerance is ABSOLUTE 1e-3 and unpivoted LU has unbounded element growth, so widening the range (or spikes) inflates intermediate magnitudes until legitimate reorder rounding exceeds 1e-3 -> false failures; shrinking range toward 0 raises near-zero-pivot probability.

extreme_values.notes: Option A (element-type extrema, current behavior): alternating -DBL_MAX/+DBL_MAX over the flattened N^2 array; for even N all rows are identical -> after elimination step k=0 (factor exactly 1, exact cancellation to 0) the k=1 pivot is 0 -> 0/0 = NaN propagates through the oracle -> harness non_finite_reference BI marker, NaN indices skipped; remaining finite indices (row 0, column-0 factors == 1) carry almost no discriminating power. No UB (IEEE double). Option B (domain extrema from lo/hi = -10/10) is trivially derivable (literals at call site) but an alternating(-10,10) matrix is EQUALLY singular - the failure is structural (unpivoted-LU domain), so no range policy fixes extreme_values for this benchmark; it needs a benchmark-level pattern policy.

spike_at.notes: spike x[k]=DBL_MAX/2 with default k=0 (ENHANCED_FILL_PARAM_K 0, enhanced-fill.hpp:82) lands on A[0][0], i.e. the FIRST PIVOT: factors A[i][0]/9e307 ~ 1e-308 are tiny, elimination proceeds on the otherwise-random [-10,10] matrix - finite and benign. For other k (spike below a diagonal) factor ~ 9e306 and row updates reach 1e307-1e308 magnitudes: possible overflow in later steps, and any finite-but-huge graded entry under ABSOLUTE tolerance 1e-3 (utilities.hpp:482) makes reorder-level rounding (ulp ~ 1e291) a false MODEL failure for candidates that do not mirror the oracle's exact operation order. Domain validity is k-dependent: benign at k=0, hazardous elsewhere.

benchmarks.adapter_notes: Pattern support is already benchmark-native via the single ENHANCED_FILL site; no adapter needed. The open question is pattern POLICY (which patterns are in the unpivoted-LU domain), not plumbing.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: No fixed buffers, no int narrowing (TEST_SIZE is size_t, heap std::vector, cpu.cc:51-55), no power-of-two requirement. Practical cost only: 3 N^2 double buffers (N=8192 -> ~1.6 GB total) and O(N^3) oracle + O(N^3) candidate per trial x MAX_VALIDATION_ATTEMPTS=2 (utilities.hpp:35). Only the global max_spec_size=4096 policy formally blocks >4096.

benchmarks.size_rationale: A (TEST_SIZE^2), b/correct/test (TEST_SIZE) all sized from TEST_SIZE (cpu.cc:72-73); construction and both solver calls use TEST_SIZE (cpu.cc:81,89,92). benchmarks.pattern_rationale: Zero ENHANCED_FILL sites (verified; shapes JSON fill_sites=0 matches). At the same size, choosing a different pattern cannot change any byte of the input - the pattern axis is dead for this benchmark as coded.
benchmarks.input_construction: createRandomLinearSystem (cpu.cc:27-39, called at cpu.cc:81): A = fillRand(-10,10) (line 28), ground-truth x = fillRand(-10,10) (line 29), b computed as b=A*x (lines 31-36), then x zeroed (line 38). validate() zeroes correct and test (cpu.cc:82-83). Oracle: unpivoted Gaussian elimination + back substitution (baseline.hpp:11-44) with a SILENT early return on an exactly-zero pivot (baseline.hpp:22-24). Comparison: reportAndCompare(correct, test, 1e-4) - ABSOLUTE tolerance (cpu.cc:103, utilities.hpp:482). NO ENHANCED_FILL site exists in this driver.
benchmarks.other_input_constructors: createRandomLinearSystem (cpu.cc:27-39): fillRand for A and ground-truth x, derived consistent RHS b=A*x; std::fill zeroing of correct/test (cpu.cc:82-83)

domain.summary: A must be nonsingular AND stably eliminable without pivoting (oracle is unpivoted). Critical hazard: an exactly-zero pivot makes the oracle return EARLY and SILENTLY (baseline.hpp:22-24), leaving correct as the pre-zeroed vector - a FINITE wrong reference that emits NO BI marker and would grade a correct candidate as a MODEL failure. Consistency invariant: b is constructed as A*x_true, so the system is always solvable when A is nonsingular. Frozen range [-10,10] random keeps all of this w.h.p.

tripwires: none in cpu.cc. The comment at cpu.cc:96-101 documents the REMOVED isnan scan (contract C1.5) - not a guard. Harness-level non_finite_reference BI marker applies via reportAndCompare, but with fully random inputs it fires only on pathological draws; no pattern can trigger it since no pattern reaches the input.

benchmarks.value_range_risk: No ENHANCED_FILL site, so spec value_range has nothing to bind to. If a site is introduced: doubles throughout, no conversion risk; numeric risk mirrors 00 (absolute 1e-4 tolerance vs elimination growth) plus the b=A*x construction squaring magnitudes (range r gives |b| up to N*r^2 = 512*100 ~ 5e4).

benchmarks.adapter_notes: A methodically clean benchmark-native adapter exists: apply the pattern to the GROUND-TRUTH solution vector x (cpu.cc:29) and keep A random and b derived - every global numeric pattern is a valid solution vector, the invariant b=A*x is preserved by construction, and validity/nonsingularity depends only on the still-random A. all_zeros/x-patterns are meaningful (does the solver recover a structured solution). Patterning A instead REQUIRES a domain policy: most global patterns make A exactly singular (zeros/same/alternating/extremes) or near-singular (ramps), which does NOT fire the BI gate here but instead trips the silent zero-pivot early return (baseline.hpp:22-24) -> false model failures; that path must not ship without a zero-pivot tripwire in the driver or oracle. Extreme/spike magnitudes on either A or x overflow b=A*x. No new pattern semantics need inventing - the ambiguity is only WHICH container carries the pattern.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: size_t sizes, heap vectors, no fixed buffers or narrowing. The globally offered static size 7 (specs.py:134) is therefore domain-INVALID for this benchmark, and any LLM-chosen non-power-of-two size <= 4096 is equally unsafe. spike_at.notes: Spike element becomes (DBL_MAX/2, DBL_MAX/2), modulus ~1.27e308. Unit-modulus twiddle rotations preserve modulus so intermediates generically stay finite (components <= modulus < DBL_MAX; complex-mult cross terms can reach |z|*sqrt(2) ~= DBL_MAX, borderline overflow in worst-case phases -> possible BI). Even when fully finite: oracle vs candidate differ by summation-order rounding at magnitude ~1e308 (1 ulp ~ 1e292), infinitely larger than the 1e-4 ABSOLUTE tolerance -> deterministic FALSE FAIL for any implementation that is not bit-identical to the oracle. The 1/N ifft scaling (~1e305 after /1024) does not change this.

domain.summary: No size restriction: the direct DFT is defined for every N including 0, 1, 2, 7 (all offered static sizes safe; verified: correctDft loops are plain 0..N-1, output resized to N). Value domain: |output| <= N*max|x|; with abs tol 1e-4, input magnitudes must stay small enough that N*max|x| rounding noise << 1e-4 (baseline [-1.0,1.0] at N=1024 -> outputs <= ~1e3, rounding ~1e-13, comfortably valid).
known_restrictions: No size restriction: the direct DFT is defined for every N including 0, 1, 2, 7 (all offered static sizes safe; verified: correctDft loops are plain 0..N-1, output resized to N). tripwires: none in cpu.cc. Harness-level A1b non-finite-reference tripwire (utilities.hpp:363-378, 422-428) fires under extreme_values: the alternating +-DBL_MAX input concentrates DFT energy at bin N/2; correctDft's partial sums at k=N/2 accumulate same-sign DBL_MAX terms -> -inf after two terms -> non-finite reference at that bin -> BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE marker, index skipped. Unlike the recursive-FFT benchmarks this is a PARTIAL BI (most other bins stay finite), so extreme_values here is a mixed BI + false-negative risk, not a fully vacuous pass.

benchmarks.value_range_risk: Always type-safe (DType stays double). Numeric risk only: output scale ~ N*max|x| vs abs tol 1e-4. At N=1024 ranges up to roughly +-1e6 keep rounding noise well under 1e-4; ranges approaching ~1e305/N overflow to inf -> partial BI. A conservative cap (e.g. |bound| <= 1e6) removes the risk.

spike_at.notes: Both x[k] and y[k] are spiked to DBL_MAX/2 (same k) -> one point at (DBL_MAX/2, DBL_MAX/2) plus 1023 random in-range points; the spike is mathematically on the hull, a meaningful adversarial input. Risk: orientation predicates on BOTH sides overflow ((c.x-a.x)*(b.y-a.y) ~ 1e3*9e307 -> inf, inf-inf -> NaN; baseline.hpp:38-40 treats NaN>0 as false). Baseline is deterministic but its pops around the spike are NaN-driven, so a candidate with an algebraically equivalent, differently associated cross product can legitimately disagree -> spurious model failure. Reference stays finite (hull vertices are input points) so the comparator BI guard never fires - failures land on the MODEL. Domain policy needed.

All are symmetric {0,1} constructions the oracle handles. Reusing numeric pattern names for cell values would invent structure semantics -> not allowed; a graph vocabulary + policy mapping is needed. benchmarks.large_size_rationale: Heap vectors, size_t sizing, no fixed buffers or power-of-two constraints. Scaling caveats: O(N^2) memory/time (N=8192 -> ~268MB), and the oracle's RECURSIVE dfs (baseline.hpp:8-16) recurses once per vertex of a component - depth up to N. At N=8192 a dense random graph makes one giant component -> ~8192-deep recursion, marginal on a 1MB default stack (Windows), comfortable on 8MB (Linux). Nothing hard-blocks moderately larger sizes; only the 4096 spec policy does, but the recursion depth must be watched in any probe.

benchmarks.adapter_notes: This is the graph benchmark where a native adapter pays off most: the current generator almost surely yields exactly 1 component at N=512/p=0.5, so component-count variation (k planted disjoint blocks, empty graph -> N components, complete graph -> 1) is both methodically clean and materially improves discrimination. All variants are symmetric {0,1}. Mapping numeric pattern names onto cells remains disallowed (invented semantics); spec-layer graph vocabulary needed. Dense variants push oracle DFS recursion toward depth N - relevant only above the current cap.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: Heap vectors, size_t sizing, no fixed buffers or power-of-two constraints; O(N^2) memory/time scaling (N=8192 -> ~268MB). Oracle uses RECURSIVE dfs (baseline.hpp:8-15) with depth up to the largest component size (~N for dense random graphs): ~8192 frames at N=8192, marginal on 1MB stacks, fine on 8MB. Only the global 4096 policy is a hard blocker today.
e2_actions: KEEP_CANDIDATE - size axis fully effective
NO_PATTERN_SUPPORT_RECOMMENDED - numeric patterns (no fill site; raw fills break invariants)
BENCHMARK_ADAPTER_NEEDED - planted-component-count generator (k blocks / empty / complete) would fix the near-constant oracle output of the current p=0.5 generator
DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - graph-pattern vocabulary at the spec layer
LARGE_SIZE_PROBE_NEEDED - quadratic memory plus recursive oracle DFS depth up to N (baseline.hpp:8-15); check stack limits before sizes >4096
benchmarks.notes: Same skeleton as 16/17. shapes JSON verified. Weak default input diversity (nearly always 1 component) is a discrimination note, not a correctness bug.

benchmarks.size_rationale: A(TEST_SIZE*TEST_SIZE) (cpu.cc:85), the per-attempt zero-reset (cpu.cc:97), the generator (cpu.cc:98), and source/dest draws (cpu.cc:99-103) all scale from TEST_SIZE, so the override scales the entire input. HOWEVER sizes 0 and 1 - both in the global static size list [0,1,2,7] - are UNSAFE for this benchmark: N=1 makes 'rand() % (N - 1)' (cpu.cc:38) and effectively 'rand() % TEST_SIZE' with the dest do-while (cpu.cc:100-103) pathological - mod-by-zero UB at cpu.cc:38 and an infinite dest loop since dest==source always; N=0 underflows the size_t 'N-1' bound at cpu.cc:32 (int i compared against SIZE_MAX) -> out-of-bounds writes through the empty nodes vector, plus rand()%0 at cpu.cc:99. EFFECTIVE for N>=2; the size axis needs a per-benchmark minimum-size guard of 2.
benchmarks.pattern_rationale: Zero ENHANCED_FILL sites (grep-verified); pattern choice cannot alter matrix, source, or dest. benchmark_shapes.json hint (fill_sites: 0) VERIFIED CORRECT.
benchmarks.input_construction: Per attempt: std::fill(A,...,0) reset (cpu.cc:97, Wave fix for audit issue #77 - generator only ADDS edges, so without the reset attempts accumulated density 0.60->0.98 and were not independent, comment cpu.cc:92-96); randomConnectedUndirectedGraph (cpu.cc:27-47): shuffled node order (std::random_shuffle, cpu.cc:30 - removed in C++17, latent build hazard) forming a spanning path (cpu.cc:32-35, guarantees connectivity), then per node rand()%(N-1) extra symmetric random edges (cpu.cc:37-46); scalars source = rand()%TEST_SIZE (cpu.cc:99), dest != source via do-while (cpu.cc:100-103). No ENHANCED_FILL.
benchmarks.other_input_constructors: randomConnectedUndirectedGraph (cpu.cc:27-47) plus scalar source/dest draws (cpu.cc:99-103); none pattern-controlled
input_types: int (symmetric adjacency matrix cells, domain {0,1}, connected graph)

Frozen family semantics per the Wave 2B comment (cpu.cc:116-126): self distance = 0, unreachable = INT_MAX, and comparison is now EXACT raw scalar - the historical normalization that aliased INT_MAX and all negatives to -1 was removed.
known_restrictions: Cells in {0,1}, symmetric; graph guaranteed CONNECTED by construction (spanning path, cpu.cc:32-35); source != dest enforced (cpu.cc:100-103); prompt/baseline comment says 'Assume the graph is connected' (baseline.hpp:10). Under the current connected-graph generator with source != dest, the reference is never INT_MAX, 0, or negative (cpu.cc:122-124), so the sentinel is currently latent; it becomes live (and exactly gradeable) only if a future adapter introduces disconnected pairs.
tripwires: none (no BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE guard; grep-verified). The Wave 2B change at cpu.cc:116-130 is a comparison-semantics fix (exact raw scalar grading), not a tripwire.

benchmarks.adapter_notes: Native axes exist and are clean IF connectivity policy is settled first: (a) density/diameter control while KEEPING the spanning-path connectivity guarantee (path graph -> max diameter, complete graph -> distance 1, sparse tree -> long paths) - fully compatible with current frozen semantics; (b) deliberately disconnected source/dest pairs - semantically DEFINED (unreachable = INT_MAX, exactly gradeable since the Wave 2B comparison fix, cpu.cc:116-126) but a change to the frozen input domain ('Assume the graph is connected', baseline.hpp:10), so it needs an explicit domain-policy decision, not just an adapter. Numeric-pattern-name reuse on cells remains disallowed. Adapter must also respect source != dest and N >= 2.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: Heap vectors, size_t sizing, ITERATIVE BFS oracle (baseline.hpp:16-40, queue-based, no recursion) - no stack hazard, no fixed buffers, no power-of-two requirement. Scaling caveats: O(N^2) memory (N=8192 -> ~268MB) and O(N^2) expected generator work (per-node rand()%(N-1) edge insertions, cpu.cc:37-46). std::random_shuffle (cpu.cc:30) is a C++17-removal build hazard independent of size. Only the global 4096 policy is a hard blocker. Separate from LARGE size: SMALL static sizes 0/1 are genuinely broken (see size_rationale).
e2_actions: KEEP_CANDIDATE - size axis effective for N >= 2

DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - (1) exclude static sizes 0 and 1 for this benchmark (UB: size_t underflow loop cpu.cc:32 at N=0, mod-by-zero cpu.cc:38/99 and infinite dest loop cpu.cc:100-103 at N=1); (2) decide whether disconnected pairs (unreachable = INT_MAX) enter the domain
NO_PATTERN_SUPPORT_RECOMMENDED - numeric patterns (no fill site; raw fills break {0,1}/symmetry/connectivity)

BENCHMARK_ADAPTER_NEEDED - connectivity-preserving diameter/density generator (path / tree / complete / Bernoulli-p plus spanning path); optionally disconnected-pair variants pending the policy decision above

FURTHER_SEMANTIC_REVIEW - edge-test divergence across the family (19's oracle treats any nonzero cell as an edge, baseline.hpp:32, vs ==1 in 15/16/18 and raw summation in 17); also std::random_shuffle (cpu.cc:30) is removed in C++17 - latent toolchain hazard
LARGE_SIZE_PROBE_NEEDED - quadratic memory/generator time only; oracle BFS is iterative and safe
benchmarks.notes: Most constrained graph benchmark: connectivity invariant, source/dest scalars, live minimum-size requirement (N >= 2), and a result-space sentinel (INT_MAX) that the Wave 2B exact-comparison fix made gradeable for future disconnected inputs. shapes JSON verified. Per-attempt matrix reset (cpu.cc:97) already fixed the attempt-independence bug (audit issue #77).

benchmarks.size_rationale: The single validate() input `image` is sized directly from TEST_SIZE (cpu.cc:55, std::vector<int> image(TEST_SIZE)); the output bins are a fixed std::array<size_t,256> (cpu.cc:56) which is a histogram property, not an input dimension. The size override scales the full relevant input.
benchmarks.pattern_rationale: The only pattern-dependent validation input (image) is entirely ENHANCED_FILL-controlled (cpu.cc:64); pattern choice changes every element. Caveat: extreme_values and spike_at always produce out-of-domain values at the default range and hence only ever exercise the baseline-incompatibility gate, never the candidate (see tripwires).
benchmarks.input_construction: validate(): image filled by ENHANCED_FILL(image, 0, 255) (cpu.cc:64), then BCAST (cpu.cc:65); bins zeroed via std::fill (cpu.cc:89-90). Driver-side reset() uses plain fillRand(ctx->image, 0, 255) (cpu.cc:29), which is timing-path only, not validation input.

fill_sites.conversion_notes: DType deduced from int literals 0/255 matches value_type int, so extreme_values yields INT_MIN/INT_MAX and spike_at yields INT_MAX/2 computed natively in int - no narrowing UB. Residual caveat: explicit_values (pattern 10) converts arbitrary doubles via static_cast<int> (enhancedFromDouble, enhanced-fill.hpp:164-170), which is UB for values outside int range; that is a values-file content risk, not a site-type mismatch. value_range overrides are cast/saturated to int (enhanced-fill.hpp:299-310).

benchmarks.other_input_constructors: none (validate input is 100% ENHANCED_FILL; reset()'s fillRand at cpu.cc:29 is the timing path only)

domain.summary: Frozen value domain is pixel intensities in [0,255] (prompt-stated; Wave-2B comment cpu.cc:67-73). Oracle correctPixelCounts indexes bins[image[i]] with no bounds check (baseline.hpp:13-17), so out-of-domain input would be an out-of-bounds write in the oracle - hence the guard.
known_restrictions: Frozen value domain is pixel intensities in [0,255] (prompt-stated; Wave-2B comment cpu.cc:67-73). Oracle correctPixelCounts indexes bins[image[i]] with no bounds check (baseline.hpp:13-17), so out-of-domain input would be an out-of-bounds write in the oracle - hence the guard.
tripwires: cpu.cc:74-87: harnessOk scan rejects any image[j] < 0 || image[j] > 255; on failure calls mismatchNoteNonFiniteReference() (cpu.cc:82, BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE transport) and `continue`s the try, so the oracle never sees invalid input and the candidate is never graded on it. Fired ALWAYS by: extreme_values (INT_MIN/INT_MAX), spike_at (INT_MAX/2 = 1073741823 > 255). Fired conditionally by: explicit_values with any value outside [0,255], and any value_range override extending outside [0,255]. Never fired at default range by: random, all_zeros (0), all_same (127), ascending/descending (integral modulo ramp stays in [0,255]), alternating (0,255), duplicate_at, sorted_except_one.

benchmarks.value_range_risk: value_range is applied as int (define mode: (decltype(lo)) cast; runtime mode: saturated to int per enhanced-fill.hpp:299-310), so no UB - but any range extending outside [0,255] makes random/ramp/alternating values out-of-domain and turns runs into BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE-only (candidate never graded). Ranges within [0,255] are safe and meaningful (e.g. narrow sub-band histograms).

The actual kernel input (vector<Point>) is thus fully derived from the two ENHANCED_FILL sites.

domain.summary: Frozen value domain 0 <= v < 2^31 (Wave-2B comment cpu.cc:67-74): below 0 the prompt's four half-open fractional intervals contain no value (negative-fraction semantics is the OPEN decision BL-08, deliberately not resolved here), and at |v| >= 2^31 the oracle's `(int) val` cast (baseline.hpp:18) is UB. tripwires: cpu.cc:75-88: harnessOk scan rejects any x[j] failing !(x[j] >= 0.0 && x[j] < 2147483648.0) - negated form also catches NaN; on failure calls mismatchNoteNonFiniteReference() (cpu.cc:83) and `continue`s -> BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE, candidate never graded on that try. Fired conditionally by: explicit_values with negative/>=2^31/NaN values, and value_range overrides with lo < 0 or hi >= 2^31. benchmarks.adapter_notes: A bool-native adapter is methodically derivable without inventing numeric-on-structure semantics: control the COUNT and POSITIONS of true bits (all-false, single-true-at-k, alternating, all-true, explicit 0/1 lists). all_zeros/alternating/duplicate_at/explicit_values(0/1) map cleanly onto that; ascending/descending/all_same/extreme_values/spike_at have no non-degenerate bool meaning and would need an explicit policy to exclude. The honest current state (no pattern support, like histogram/23's string input) is also defensible and is what benchmark_shapes.json records.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: O(n) fill, O(n) XOR reduce, heap-allocated vector<bool> plus an O(n) char shadow copy under MPI (cpu.cc:28). No fixed buffers, no int narrowing of the size (loop indices are int vs size_t TEST_SIZE - benign below 2^31), no power-of-two requirement, no complexity blowup. Only the global max_spec_size=4096 policy caps sizes.
e2_actions: KEEP_CANDIDATE - size axis only: size override is fully effective
NO_PATTERN_SUPPORT_RECOMMENDED - current honest state (0 fill sites, explicit_values disabled) mirrors the histogram/23 reference case
DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - only if bool patterns are wanted: define a bool-native vocabulary (true-density/parity/position of true bits) instead of reusing the numeric pattern ids
benchmarks.notes: vector<bool> is the special proxy-reference specialization; ENHANCED_FILL was presumably never applied here partly for that reason (fillRand's x[i] = val works via proxy, but the harness template has no is_same_v<DType,bool> branch, so a retrofit would need care - bool falls into the is_integral_v branches, where fillRand's rand() % (max - min) with max-min==1 is degenerate-but-defined: always 0). Exact-equality scalar bool comparison; MAX_VALIDATION_ATTEMPTS defaults to 2 (utilities.hpp:34-36).

benchmarks.size_rationale: The single input x is sized TEST_SIZE (cpu.cc:116) and fully refilled per trial by ENHANCED_FILL (cpu.cc:125); the frozen D6 comparator even scales its tolerance with the ACTUAL length, eps_rel = 8*n*u with n = x.size() (cpu.cc:69, 139). TEST_SIZE=0: oracle returns the empty-product identity 1.0 (baseline.hpp:16) and epsRel becomes 0, so rule E demands a bit-exact 1.0 from the candidate - a graded (not BI) unpinned-empty-convention edge.
benchmarks.pattern_rationale: The one and only validation input is fully ENHANCED_FILL-controlled (cpu.cc:125); every pattern id changes the whole input. Matches benchmark_shapes.json (1 site, n elements, explicit_values enabled).
benchmarks.input_construction: ENHANCED_FILL(x, 1.0, 100.0) per trial (cpu.cc:125) then BCAST(x, DOUBLE) (cpu.cc:126). Timed path uses fillRand(ctx->x, 1.0, 100.0) (cpu.cc:90).

fill_sites.conversion_notes: DType deduced from the double literals equals the element type; every pattern value (including +-DBL_MAX extremes and DBL_MAX/2 spike) is representable - no narrowing, no UB. Hazards on this benchmark are all on the DOMAIN axis (overflow/underflow of the PRODUCT), not the type axis.

extreme_values.notes: Option A (element-type extrema, current behavior): alternating -DBL_MAX/+DBL_MAX. The serial oracle's left-to-right inclusive_scan stays finite ({-DBL_MAX, 0} alternating, exact cancellation), so the reference is finite and the candidate IS graded. Hazard: any reassociating implementation (inherent in parallel scans; formally even std::inclusive_scan permits arbitrary association) can sum two -DBL_MAX terms -> -inf; finite reference + non-finite candidate = graded FAIL (utilities.hpp Contract A1b case 2) - a correct-under-reals parallel scan can be unfairly failed. Also, with values at magnitude 1.8e308 the ABSOLUTE 1e-6 tolerance means only bit-exact agreement passes (ULP at DBL_MAX ~ 2e292); cancellations here happen to be exact so left-to-right candidates pass. Option B (domain extrema from lo/hi, +-100) is trivially derivable but coincides with pattern 5 (alternating). No tripwire fires (there is none).

spike_at.notes: Random [-100,100] fill plus x[k]=DBL_MAX/2 (~8.99e307). Prefixes before k are ordinary small sums; prefixes at/after k round to exactly DBL_MAX/2 (the +-100-scale contributions are absorbed below one ULP) for oracle and candidate alike, so the absolute 1e-6 tolerance is not stressed. Single spike cannot overflow (would need two ~DBL_MAX/2 terms). A well-behaved, meaningful magnitude-robustness probe.

spike_at.notes: x[k]=DBL_MAX/2 makes every prefix from k onward ~DBL_MAX/2; accumulate sums (n-k) such terms, overflowing to +inf whenever n-k >= 3 (i.e. any k <= n-3) -> non-finite reference -> BI-only, candidate ungraded. Only k in {n-2, n-1} stays finite (DBL_MAX or DBL_MAX/2 plus noise) - and k=n-2 sits exactly at DBL_MAX, one rounding away from inf. Effectively spike_at is baseline-gate-only for all practically chosen k.

extreme_values.notes: UNGUARDED UB: Option A extrema give x = INT_MIN, INT_MAX, INT_MIN, ...; in the oracle's inner loop currSum goes 0 -> INT_MIN -> -1 (INT_MIN+INT_MAX) -> -1+INT_MIN = signed overflow = UB at the third element, i.e. for every n >= 3 (default 1024, static size 7). The candidate's own accumulation is equally exposed. There is no tripwire and no harness net (ints are always 'finite', so the non-finite-reference contract cannot catch this) - selecting extreme_values on this benchmark executes UB in the baseline itself. scan/33 got a Wave-2B guard for the identical hazard; scan/34 did not. Option B lo/hi extrema (+-100) are derivable and safe (window sums bounded by 100n).

spike_at.notes: Single spike INT_MAX/2 = 1073741823 among random [-100,100] values: any window sum is bounded by 2^30-1 + 100n < INT_MAX for n < ~1.07e7, so at all frozen/plausible sizes there is NO overflow - oracle and candidate stay well-defined and the expected answer is dominated by the spike. Unlike scan/33 (where the tripwire kills it) spike_at here is domain-valid and a genuinely meaningful probe. Conditional only on n staying below ~1e7 and on no second extreme value.

CAVEAT: size 0 is NOT guarded - attempt i==1 executes x[rand()%x.size()] and y[rand()%y.size()] (cpu.cc:75-76), a modulo-by-zero SIGFPE on empty vectors; with numTries=10 (cpu.cc:66) attempt 1 is always reached, so spec static size 0 crashes. benchmarks.pattern_rationale: Both relevant containers are ENHANCED_FILL-controlled, so pattern choice changes ALL pattern-dependent input components. Structural caveat: the global one-pattern-per-run design gives x and y identical content under every deterministic pattern, which makes xorContains structurally false for every val (val in both or in neither) - the XOR-true branch is then exercised ONLY by random-based patterns (random, duplicate_at, spike_at with independent random fills). This is a discrimination limitation, not invalidity: outcomes remain deterministic and correctly graded.
benchmarks.input_construction: validate() builds std::vector<int> x(TEST_SIZE) and y(TEST_SIZE) via two ENHANCED_FILL calls (cpu.cc:71-72); scalar val = rand()%200-100 (cpu.cc:73); attempt i==1 plants val into BOTH vectors (cpu.cc:74-77, guaranteed 'in both -> false' case). Oracle correctXorContains (baseline.hpp:15-20) is two std::find calls XORed.

known_restrictions: Frozen field domains: startTime 0..100, duration 1..10, value [-1,1] (reset cpu.cc:106-108 = validate cpu.cc:154-156). The duration>=1 invariant exists only as a fill range — nothing downstream depends on it (duration is payload). Sort key is startTime only.
tripwires: Two BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE paths: (1) the Wave-2B reference selftest (cpu.cc:174-185) — fires if correctSortByStartTime's output violates the frozen invariants; the oracle (baseline.hpp:15-19, plain std::sort on an int key) cannot violate them for any offered pattern. (2) INDIRECT and REAL under the current type-unsafe value site: extreme_values (pattern 6) and spike_at (pattern 9) practically put +-inf/inf into the float value field; inside sameRecordMultiset the reference-side reportAndCompareEq(aVal,bVal) then emits BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE: non_finite_reference and SKIPS those indices (utilities.hpp:425-428) — during both the selftest and candidate grading. Both patterns still 'pass' functionally (selftest returns true, key/duration fields fully graded) but every such run is flagged baseline-incompatible at the parser: patterns 6 and 9 are currently a baseline-gate-only risk for this benchmark, on top of the formal UB.

benchmarks.value_range_risk: Moderate, two distinct issues: (1) a single global value_range overrides ALL THREE sites with the same LO/HI (cast per-site to int, int, double) — the per-field domain distinctions (0..100 vs 1..10 vs -1..1) collapse; semantically survivable (key comparator and payload are total over int/float) but it silently voids the duration>=1 domain. (2) On the double-literal value site, any range beyond +-FLT_MAX re-creates the double->float UB even for benign patterns. Fixing the site types removes (2); (1) is a spec-design property.

benchmarks.size_rationale: input(TEST_SIZE) (cpu.cc:64) is the entire instance and is filled per-trial by fillRandWithZeroes (cpu.cc:68); size scales everything. Size 0 degenerates gracefully (empty vectors compare equal).
benchmarks.pattern_rationale: Zero ENHANCED_FILL sites: at the same size, choosing a different global pattern cannot change one bit of the input — fillRandWithZeroes ignores the pattern machinery entirely. This is the family's deliberate no-pattern benchmark (analogous to histogram/23's string input), and benchmark_shapes.json records it as such (fill_sites: 0).
benchmarks.input_construction: vector<int> input(TEST_SIZE) built by the benchmark-specific fillRandWithZeroes (cpu.cc:25-33): x[i]=rand(), then set to 0 with probability 4/5 (`if (rand() % 5) x[i] = 0;` cpu.cc:29-31) — i.e. ~80% zeros, ~20% uniform non-negative values in 0..RAND_MAX. Exact element-wise grading against the oracle via reportAndCompareEq(correctResult, testResult, input) (cpu.cc:81); the oracle's output is unique (sorted non-zero multiset written back into the non-zero positions, baseline.hpp:7-24), so exact comparison is sound.

sentinels: 0 is the load-bearing semantic sentinel: zero elements must remain in place while non-zeros are sorted around them. Any input-generation scheme must control zero placement deliberately; a generic numeric pattern that happens to produce or remove zeros would silently change the task difficulty.
tripwires: none — no BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE guard exists in this cpu.cc; reportAndCompareEq's non-finite path is unreachable for int, and there is no size or selftest guard. No offered pattern can fire anything because no pattern reaches the input at all.

benchmarks.adapter_notes: A benchmark-NATIVE adapter is methodically clean along the axes the task itself defines: (a) zero DENSITY (currently hard-coded ~80%, cpu.cc:29-31), (b) zero PLACEMENT (random / blocked / edges / none / all), (c) non-zero value arrangement (random / ascending / descending / one spike). None of these breaks validity or forces BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE — the oracle is total over any int vector and the exact-comparison grading stays sound for every density including 0% and 100% zeros. Some global patterns even have natural native readings (all_zeros -> all elements zero, trivially valid; ascending -> ascending non-zeros with zeros interspersed; spike_at -> one huge non-zero; extreme_values -> INT_MIN/INT_MAX non-zeros at the frozen density). What is NOT derivable mechanically is the mapping policy: which of the 11 global pattern IDs maps to which (density, placement, arrangement) combination, and what the default density is for each — that is a documented policy decision, not new numeric-on-structure semantics. Without that decision, the honest state is the current one: no pattern support.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: input is one O(n) vector; oracle collects non-zeros, sorts O(n log n), writes back (baseline.hpp:7-24). `int i` loops in fillRandWithZeroes (cpu.cc:27) and the oracle (baseline.hpp:18) cap at 2^31 — theoretical only. Coverage caveat, not a blocker: on Windows RAND_MAX=32767, so at large n the ~20% non-zero values are drawn from only 32768 distinct values (heavy duplication — harmless because the correct output is still unique). Only the global max_spec_size=4096 policy blocks >4096.
e2_actions: KEEP_CANDIDATE — the size axis is fully effective and cheap; the benchmark is valuable for size scaling alone
NO_PATTERN_SUPPORT_RECOMMENDED — for the current spec layer, record honestly (histogram/23-style) that global numeric patterns do not and cannot apply to the zero-structured input as wrapped today

BENCHMARK_ADAPTER_NEEDED — only if pattern coverage is wanted: a native (zero-density, zero-placement, non-zero-arrangement) adapter is clean and BI-free, but requires the pattern-ID mapping policy below

DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED — define the mapping from global pattern IDs to native axes and the default zero density; also decide whether the harness's never-negative values (rand() >= 0, contradicting the prompt's example with -1) should stay frozen or be widened
benchmarks.notes: benchmark_shapes.json entry verified correct (fill_sites 0, explicit_values disabled, 'deliberately not wrapped'). Exact element-wise comparison is sound here because the correct output is unique (no tie-order freedom: equal values are indistinguishable, zero positions are fixed). The harness-vs-prompt discrepancy (no negative values ever generated) slightly narrows what candidates are tested on — e.g. a candidate that mishandles negative non-zeros would pass.

benchmarks.size_rationale: Every validation input is derived from TEST_SIZE: buildDominantSystem(inst, TEST_SIZE) constructs the whole COO system, b and x_gen at that size (cpu.cc:239); x_test/x_ref are sized TEST_SIZE (cpu.cc:227); per-row nnz = max(2, round(SPARSE_LA_SPARSITY*N)) capped at N scales with N (cpu.cc:98-104). No static or other-sized component remains.
benchmarks.pattern_rationale: Zero ENHANCED_FILL sites in validate() (verified; matches benchmark_shapes.json:406-412 fill_sites=0). Same size + different pattern produces bit-identical validation input: the D4 constructor draws exclusively from rand(). Patterns COULD in principle have numeric semantics here (values are doubles), but the frozen D4 validity invariants (dominance, exact integer b=A*x_gen) deliberately exclude generic fills, so the honest grade is NONE, not NOT_APPLICABLE.
benchmarks.input_construction: D4 frozen validation construction pareval_harness::buildDominantSystem (cpu.cc:81-155): square duplicate-free integer COO, diagonal present in every row; off-diagonal lattice values +-[1,4] (cpu.cc:128-129); strict dominance |a_ii| = S_i + max(1, ceil(S_i/4)) i.e. gamma=1.25 (cpu.cc:137-142); independent ground truth x_gen integer in [-8,8] (cpu.cc:93-96); b = A*x_gen accumulated exactly in long long (cpu.cc:124-153). Draws from the unseeded rand() stream; BCASTs pin root arrays (cpu.cc:240-244); assembleSortedCoo sorts row/column (cpu.cc:157-163, 245). The timed path (reset/createRandomLinearSystem, cpu.cc:167-196) uses fillRand and is unchanged/not graded.
benchmarks.other_input_constructors: pareval_harness::buildDominantSystem (rand()-driven D4 constructor, cpu.cc:81-155); pareval_harness::assembleSortedCoo (cpu.cc:157-163); timed-path-only fillRand calls (cpu.cc:170-172, 182) which never feed validate().

benchmarks.adapter_notes: The D4 construction is fully documented in-source (topology: per-row nnz max(2,round(0.1N)) incl. diagonal, duplicate-free; values: lattice +-[1,4], dominance formula; RHS: b=A*x_gen exact; invariants: dominance gamma=1.25, exactness <2^53). A benchmark-native adapter could pattern the FREE choices without breaking validity: x_gen profile (all_zeros/all_same/ascending within [-8,8]), off-diagonal sign/magnitude profiles within [1,4], diagonal sign profile - b is recomputed exactly afterwards, so every such variation stays domain-valid and cannot fire the tripwires. Applying numeric patterns to the COO structure (rows/columns) would be invented semantics - excluded. Requires an explicit policy decision on which free axes map to which global pattern names.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: No fixed buffers, no stack arrays, no power-of-two requirement; loop counters int in the timed path only. But beyond the global max_spec_size=4096 policy, the oracle correctSolveLinearSystem is dense O(N^3) Gaussian elimination with an O(N^2) vector<vector<double>> matrix (baseline.hpp:17,29-58), buildDominantSystem is O(N^2) (per-row std::fill of used[N], cpu.cc:111), and MAX_VALIDATION_ATTEMPTS=2 (utilities.hpp:35) doubles it: at N=8192 that is ~2x5.5e11 flops plus ~0.5GB dense scratch - a practical compute blocker on top of the spec policy, not a correctness blocker.
e2_actions: EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE - generic ENHANCED_FILL patterns: zero fill sites, patterns are inert by construction
BENCHMARK_ADAPTER_NEEDED - if pattern coverage is wanted, a D4-aware constructor adapter over x_gen/lattice free choices is the only clean route
DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - map of global pattern names onto D4 free axes must be frozen before any adapter
LARGE_SIZE_PROBE_NEEDED - O(N^3) dense oracle x2 attempts: measure wall time before raising the 4096 cap
benchmarks.notes: benchmark_shapes.json entry (lines 406-412) verified correct: fill_sites=0, explicit_values false. Grading is against the independent x_gen at tolerance 1e-3 (cpu.cc:269-277), never against the numeric oracle; the oracle only serves as a finiteness selftest whose failure is routed to BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE, not to the candidate.

benchmarks.size_rationale: All main-trial extents derive from TEST_SIZE: nVals_A = nVals_X = TEST_SIZE*TEST_SIZE*SPARSE_LA_SPARSITY (cpu.cc:162-163), Y buffers TEST_SIZE*TEST_SIZE (cpu.cc:169), square M=K=N=TEST_SIZE in both oracle and candidate calls (cpu.cc:224,227). The additional A8/I13 nonsquare probe also scales from TEST_SIZE (nsM=TEST_SIZE, nsK=TEST_SIZE/4, nsN=TEST_SIZE/2, cpu.cc:246-251). Nothing stays static.
benchmarks.pattern_rationale: Both main-trial value arrays are ENHANCED_FILL-controlled (cpu.cc:185-186), but a graded input component escapes the pattern: the A8/I13 nonsquare probe's value arrays use plain fillRand (cpu.cc:263-264) yet its comparison (cpu.cc:296) can fail the candidate. So a pattern spec controls the main trials only, not all pattern-relevant value inputs of the validate() run. Index arrays are structural by frozen I5 policy (not counted against the pattern).
benchmarks.input_construction: Main trials: unique (row,column) coordinates per matrix via pareval_harness::drawUniqueCoordinates rejection sampling on rand() (cpu.cc:56-80, called 181-184; frozen I5 duplicate contract), VALUE arrays via ENHANCED_FILL (cpu.cc:185-186), assembled and row/column-sorted into COO (cpu.cc:213-221). Nonsquare probe: same unique-coordinate draw within nsM x nsK / nsK x nsN (cpu.cc:259-262) but values via plain fillRand (cpu.cc:263-264).

fill_sites.conversion_notes: double->double, no conversion. extreme_values assigns +-DBL_MAX, spike_at DBL_MAX/2 - representable, no UB.
double->double, no conversion.

benchmarks.other_input_constructors: pareval_harness::drawUniqueCoordinates for all four index arrays (cpu.cc:181-184, 259-262) - structural, deliberately not pattern-fillable (comment cpu.cc:176-180: index-pattern policy queued to the enhanced wave); fillRand for the nonsquare probe's nsA_values/nsX_values (cpu.cc:263-264).

domain.summary: Values frozen to [-1,1] (both fill sites and the probe's fillRand); unique (row,column) per matrix (I5, cpu.cc:49-55); indices valid by construction and re-checked (cooIndicesInRange); nnz = floor(0.1*rows*cols); comparison tolerance absolute 1e-4 (cpu.cc:231,296).
known_restrictions: Values frozen to [-1,1] (both fill sites and the probe's fillRand); unique (row,column) per matrix (I5, cpu.cc:49-55); indices valid by construction and re-checked (cooIndicesInRange); nnz = floor(0.1*rows*cols); comparison tolerance absolute 1e-4 (cpu.cc:231,296).
tripwires: (1) drawUniqueCoordinates returns false when count > cells (cpu.cc:60-62) - unreachable for derived nnz. (2) cooIndicesInRange guard (cpu.cc:86-94) checked at 199-201 and 273-275; failure -> mismatchNoteNonFiniteReference() BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE marker and trial skip (cpu.cc:202-207) / probe skip (cpu.cc:276-279) - required because the oracle writes Y[a.row*N+x.column] unguarded (baseline.hpp:22, comment cpu.cc:82-85). Patterns cannot fire these (they touch values only). (3) reportAndCompare per-index non-finite REFERENCE -> BI marker + index skipped (utilities.hpp:425-428): THIS one is pattern-reachable - extreme_values makes every oracle product (+-DBL_MAX)*(+-DBL_MAX) overflow to inf, so extreme_values is a baseline-gate-only pattern for the main trials (candidate effectively ungraded at all touched Y indices); spike_at fires it only when A's spike column equals X's spike row ((DBL_MAX/2)^2 -> inf).

benchmarks.value_range_risk: Spec value_range binds ENHANCED_FILL_LO/HI cast to decltype(lo)=double (enhanced-fill.hpp:450-452) - no truncation UB. But any widened range re-freezes the numeric domain: |lo|,|hi| > ~1e154 lets a single product overflow in the oracle (BI), and any range with values >> 1e-4 magnifies the absolute-tolerance brittleness of the 1e-4 epsilon. The nonsquare probe ignores the range (fillRand -1..1 hardcoded, cpu.cc:263-264), creating a mixed-domain validate().

extreme_values.notes: Option A element-type extrema = +-DBL_MAX (DType=double, enhanced-fill.hpp:130-132): representable, no UB, but leaves the frozen [-1,1] domain by ~308 orders of magnitude. Oracle Y accumulation overflows to inf on every A/X match -> per-index BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE skip (utilities.hpp:425-428); unmatched Y cells stay 0 and grade trivially. Net effect: main trials grade almost nothing (baseline-gate-only risk), while the nonsquare probe (fillRand values) still grades normally. Secondary risk: any FINITE huge reference value meets the absolute 1e-4 epsilon (cpu.cc:231) - a 1-ulp ordering difference at 1e308 scale is a spurious candidate FAIL. Option B domain extrema from lo/hi (+-1.0) are already exactly what the alternating pattern (5) produces - derivable and safe.

spike_at.notes: DBL_MAX/2 spike in both A_values and X_values (same pattern applied per site). Products spike*random <= DBL_MAX/2 stay finite and each Y cell receives at most one spike product (unique coordinates), so overflow only occurs if A's spike entry column == X's spike entry row: (DBL_MAX/2)^2 = inf -> per-index BI. Otherwise trials grade, but graded magnitudes ~1e308 against absolute epsilon 1e-4 make candidate/oracle summation-order differences a spurious-FAIL hazard. Domain: DBL_MAX/2 is far outside the frozen [-1,1].

benchmarks.large_size_rationale: Beyond the global 4096 spec cap: the oracle correctSpmm is O(nnz_A*nnz_X) - a full cross product of the two COO lists (baseline.hpp:19-25). nnz scales as 0.1*N^2, so oracle work is O(0.01*N^4): at N=4096 that is ~2.8e12 element pairs per trial (x MAX_VALIDATION_ATTEMPTS=2) - a hard practical wall well before memory does (Y is N^2 doubles = 134MB at 4096; drawUniqueCoordinates used[] is N^2 bytes). Also int loop counters over nnz (cpu.cc:213,218) overflow only past nnz=2^31 (N~146k) - not the binding constraint. No fixed buffers, no power-of-two requirement.

extreme_values.notes: Option A element extrema +-DBL_MAX in values, x AND y: representable (no UB), but ~308 orders outside the frozen [-1,1] domain. Oracle: beta*y stays finite (|beta|<=1) but every A-entry contribution alpha*value*x overflows -> inf in every row that has an nnz (at 10% density and N=128, nearly all rows) -> per-index BI skips: largely a baseline-gate-only trial. Finite untouched rows grade beta*y, computed identically by any reasonable candidate (single multiply), so spurious-FAIL risk is low there but nonzero given the absolute 1e-4 epsilon at 1e308 magnitudes. Option B domain extrema (+-1.0 from lo/hi) are derivable - pattern alternating already realizes them safely.

spike_at.notes: Spike DBL_MAX/2 lands in values[k], x[k] and y[k] (same k across the three sites). Individual contributions stay <= DBL_MAX/2 (|alpha|,|beta|<=1), and unique coordinates spread column-k products across distinct rows, so sums of two half-max terms stay <= DBL_MAX; overflow needs the A-spike entry to hit column k (alpha*(DBL_MAX/2)*(DBL_MAX/2) -> inf) - conditional, draw-dependent BI. Main hazard is again the absolute 1e-4 epsilon: graded finite values at ~1e308 make any accumulation-order divergence a spurious candidate FAIL. Domain: far outside [-1,1].

benchmarks.adapter_notes: The D5 construction is fully documented in-source (factor topology: band k density-preserving; values: lattice +-[1,4]; pivots 2^e, e in [0,5]; invariant: A=L*U exact < 2^53, full-band duplicate-free COO). A native adapter could pattern the FREE choices - off-diagonal sign/magnitude profiles within [1,4], pivot-exponent profiles within [0,5] (all_same/ascending/extreme-of-lattice) - and recompute A exactly afterwards, preserving every invariant and the exact-division property. Patterning A's values directly, or the COO structure, would sever A=L*U or invent structure semantics - excluded. Requires a frozen policy mapping global pattern names onto these factor-lattice axes; bandwidth itself is a frozen density decision (cpu.cc:73-74) and should stay out of pattern scope.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: Beyond the global 4096 spec cap: validate() holds SIX dense N^2 double arrays (L_true/U_true in the instance, cpu.cc:107-108; L_ref/U_ref/L_test/U_test, cpu.cc:215-216) = 48*N^2 bytes - 805MB at N=4096, 3.2GB at 8192; the oracle correctLuFactorize is dense O(N^3) (baseline.hpp:24-40) and the band product in buildLuGroundTruth is O(N*k^2) ~ O(0.0025*N^3), all x MAX_VALIDATION_ATTEMPTS=2. Compute and memory blow up together on top of the spec policy. No fixed buffers, no int narrowing on sized loops in validate, no power-of-two size requirement (only pivot VALUES are powers of two). Note the family-smallest default (64) already reflects the O(N^3) cost.
e2_actions: EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE - generic ENHANCED_FILL patterns: zero fill sites, patterns inert; direct A-value fills would falsify the graded ground truth
BENCHMARK_ADAPTER_NEEDED - D5-aware factor-lattice adapter (sign/magnitude/pivot-exponent profiles, A recomputed exactly) is the only clean pattern route
DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - mapping of global pattern names onto D5 free axes must be frozen first
LARGE_SIZE_PROBE_NEEDED - 6x dense N^2 memory + O(N^3) oracle x2 attempts: measure before raising sizes toward 4096, which is already ~800MB dense scratch
benchmarks.notes: benchmark_shapes.json entry (lines 444-450) verified correct: fill_sites=0, explicit_values false. Grading compares candidate L/U against the constructed factors at 1e-3 (cpu.cc:269-273); the Doolittle oracle serves only as a finiteness selftest routed to BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE on failure. isCooEqual (cpu.cc:47-59) exists but is unused by validate() - dead helper for this path.

benchmarks.value_range_risk: Casts saturate (no conversion UB), but semantics degrade fast: any range beyond {0,1} makes the oracle grade candidates on its arbitrary raw-sum treatment of non-binary cells (e.g. ascending/descending ramps over [0,2] mix 1s and 2s, where a count-alive-neighbors candidate diverges from the raw-sum oracle); ranges with |values| > ~INT_MAX/8 re-expose the unguarded overflow UB. Note the current default lo/hi (0,2) already put 2s in play for alternating/ramp - only the random patterns stay binary (hi-exclusive).

extreme_values.notes: HIGHEST-SEVERITY FINDING of the family. Option A element extrema (INT_MIN/INT_MAX alternating by linear index) feed the oracle's raw 8-neighbor int sum: for any N >= 3 same-parity neighbor pairs exist (even N: vertical neighbors; odd N: diagonals), so INT_MIN+INT_MIN / INT_MAX+INT_MAX overflows - undefined behavior in correctGameOfLife (baseline.hpp:27-51) with NO guard and no BI transport. Needs a 51-style in-domain scan ({0,1}) or per-benchmark exclusion of extreme_values before this pattern is ever offered. Option B domain extrema from lo/hi ({0,2}) avoid overflow but still inject the out-of-domain value 2.

spike_at.notes: Single INT_MAX/2 spike over a {0,1} random background: each neighbor sum contains at most one spike, so max sum = INT_MAX/2 + 7 - no overflow, fully defined. The spiked cell is treated as dead (==1 false); its 8 neighbors get sum >= INT_MAX/2 != 3, so their outputs are deterministically 0. Out of the frozen {0,1} domain; discriminates candidates that use nonzero-as-alive or bool conversion - whether that discrimination is wanted is a policy call.

domain.summary: Implicit x != 0: the operation is 1 - 1/x (baseline.hpp:11). The frozen continuous fillRand(-50.0,50.0) draw hits exact 0.0 with probability ~0, but deterministic patterns hit it: (a) all_zeros fills the ENTIRE vector with 0.0 (enhanced-fill.hpp:185); (b) all_same fills the ENTIRE vector with the midpoint of [-50,50] = exactly 0.0 (enhanced-fill.hpp:148,188); (c) ascending/descending and sorted_except_one use the float ramp lo+(hi-lo)*(pos/(n-1)) (enhanced-fill.hpp:113) which is exactly 0.0 whenever pos/(n-1) is exactly 0.5 in binary - true at offered static size 7 (pos=3, 3/6=0.5) and at n=1025 (512/1024), NOT at the default 1024 (would need pos=511.5). At x=0.0: 1/0.0=+inf, result -inf - IEEE-defined, not UB, but the comparator std::abs(x-y)>eps (utilities.hpp:491) is NaN-absorbing: (-inf)-(-inf)=NaN which compares 'equal', so a candidate producing NaN (or any non-finite value) at those indices silently PASSES against the baseline's -inf. Singular inputs therefore degrade the oracle's discriminative power rather than crashing.

extreme_values.notes: Option A extrema INT_MIN/INT_MAX: oracle referenceIsPowerOfTwo (baseline.hpp:21-23) returns false for both with no UB (short-circuit protects INT_MIN - 1 from ever evaluating); the prompt-provided candidate predicate has the identical form. The Wave-fixed candidate-independent oracle makes this the family's cleanest extreme_values benchmark. Option B extrema (1/1025) also trivially safe.

spike_at.notes: Spike INT_MAX/2 = 1073741823 = 2^30 - 1, not a power of two -> false; a genuinely discriminative near-boundary value (2^30 itself IS a power of two). Rest random in [1,1025]. Safe.

explicit_values.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE (E2: validate value magnitudes against element type and frozen domain - specs.py currently validates neither)
explicit_values.notes: values are arbitrary spec-supplied doubles; for int containers enhancedFromDouble static_casts them (out-of-range = UB) and the spec layer does not validate magnitudes

benchmarks.adapter_notes: Pattern effect already EFFECTIVE on the sole input; mask is an output by design.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: Heap vector + vector<bool>, O(n); only structural quirk is the oracle's int loop index (for (int i = 0; i < x.size(); i++), baseline.hpp:34) which would only matter beyond INT_MAX elements - irrelevant at any plausible size. Only max_spec_size=4096 blocks >4096.
e2_actions: KEEP_CANDIDATE: total predicate + hardened candidate-independent oracle make every offered pattern safe, including extreme_values and spike_at
benchmarks.notes: reportAndCompareEq on vector<bool> (cpu.cc:72) is exact; no tolerance or NaN issues. The oracle was explicitly fixed to not call the candidate's isPowerOfTwo (baseline.hpp:14-20), removing the historical candidate-dependent-reference defect.
